full_judgment:
These two Rules issued in Civil Revision No. 26 of 1985 and Civil Revision No. 27 of 1985 at the instance of pre-emptor Abdul Malek are directed against one and the same judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 196 of 1982 and Miscellaneous Appeal No. 197 of 1982 on 12.9.84. by the Subordinate Judge, Jhalakati affirming the analogous judgment and order passed on 20.9.82 by the Munsif, Jhalakati disallowing Miscellaneous Case Nos. 186 of 1975 and 187 or 1975 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Both the Rules are being disposed of by this judgment. 

 2. Miscellaneous Case No. 186 of 1975 relates to 0.62-1/2 acre and Miscellaneous Case No. 187 of 1975 relates to 0.31-1/4 acre of lands out of plot No. 1082 appertaining to SA Khatian No. 1283 of mouja Grangal Rajpassa under police station Jhalakati. Both the cases were filed by petitioner Abdul Maleq against the successors-in-interest (OPs No.1-4) of vendee Mozaharuddin in respect of transfer made by Pakkhi Bibi and by her son Abdul Mannan respectfully. 

 3. Petitioner Abdul Maleq and others instituted on 31.3.75 Title Suit No. 137 or 1975 in the first court of Subordinate Judge, Barisal against Pakkhi Bibi and others claiming some interest in the lands of SA Khatian Nos. 1283 and 2149 of mouza Grangal Rajpassa. On 20.4.75 a petition dated 28.4.75 purported to have been verified by Pakkhi Bibi by the pen of her son-in-law Aynal Kha was filed claiming exemption from the costs of the suit on the ground that she had already transferred her interest in favour of Mozaharuddin and her son Abdul Mannan. Thereafter on 22.8.75 the petitioner filed the instant two pre-emption cases on deposit of the amounts of the consideration money claiming that he was a co-sharer, that he was a bonafide cultivator and that the kabala lands added to the lands already held by him would not exceed the prescribed limit, on the allegations in Miscellaneous Case No. 186 of 1975 that Pakkhi Bibi sold 0.62-1/2 acre or lands for a consideration of Tk. 4000/- and in Miscellaneous Case No. 187 of 1975 Abdul Mannan sold 0.31-1/4 acre of lands for a consideration of Tk. 2000/-, both out of plot No. 1082 in favour of Mozaharuddin, predecessor-in-interest of opposite party Nos. 1-4 without any notice to him. The lands were already in possession of Nur Mohammad, husband of opposite party No. 2 Lutfunnessa on the strength of a Meyadi Patta and as such he had no scope to know about the disputed transfers. On getting copy of Pakkhi Bibi's petition dated 30.4.75 he made search in the Registry Office, took out certificate copies of the two disputed kabalas on 12.8.75 and then filed the pre-emption cases. 

 11. From the above analysis it is clear that the court below has committed an error of law in finding that the petition dated 30.4.75 was not filed in or in connection with Title Suit No. 137 of 1975 as contended by the pre-emptor. This relates to the petitioner's first knowledge only in connection with Miscellaneous Case No. 186 of 1975 and the court below has come to an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice in holding that the said Miscellaneous Case is barred by limitation. As regards the other case i.e. Miscellaneous Case No. 187 of 1975, the courts below have been perfectly justified in finding limitation against the pre-emptor. In such view of the matter the impugned judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 186 of 1975 can not be sustained and is liable to be set aside. The court has not however committed any error of law in disallowing pre-emption in the other case on the ground of limitation and as such the judgment and order passed in that case is not liable to be interfered with. 

 In the result the Rule issued in Civil Revision No. 26 of 1985 is made absolute and the Rule issued in Civil Revision 27 of 1985 is discharged without any order as to costs. The judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 196 of 1982 by the learned Subordinate Judge, Jhalakati is set aside and the pre-emption case No. 186 of 1975 is allowed. The right, title and interest in the disputed 0.62-1/2 acre of lands accrued to the vendee Mozaharuddin by virtue of the transfer dated 14.3.68 do vest in the pre-emptor Abdul Maleq and he does get possession therein forthwith. The opposite party Nos. 1-4 are at liberty to withdraw the amount in deposit in connection with the said transfer.
